t.1.18.1: Having heard that wondrous and expansive speech of the lion among kings, the greatly radiant Viśvāmitra, his hair bristling with joy, spoke in reply.
t.1.18.2: O tiger among kings, this is worthy of you alone and of no one else on earth, you who were born of a great lineage and have Vasiṣṭha as your guide.
t.1.18.3: As for the words that lie in my heart, make a firm resolve to carry out that task, O tiger among kings, and be true to your promise.
t.1.18.5: When my vow, often undertaken, was nearing its completion, these two rākṣasas, Mārīca and Subāhu, mighty and well trained, rained down upon that altar a flood of flesh and blood.
t.1.18.4: O bull among men, I have undertaken a sacred observance for the sake of attaining success, but two rākṣasas who can take any form at will are creating obstacles to it.
t.1.18.6: When my firm resolve in that observance had thus been shaken off and brought to nothing, I, worn out by my toil and disheartened, withdrew from that place.
t.1.18.7: Nor does my mind incline to let loose my anger, O king, for such is the nature of that observance that no curse may be uttered during it.
t.1.18.8: O tiger among kings, you ought to give me your own eldest son Rāma, the hero of true valor who still wears the side-locks of youth.
t.1.18.10: And I shall bestow upon him manifold good fortune, there is no doubt, by which he will attain renown throughout all the three worlds.
t.1.18.9: For he, protected by me, is able by his own divine power to destroy even those rākṣasas who are the disrupters of the sacrifice.
t.1.18.11: Once they encounter Rāma, those two will be unable to stand their ground in any way, and no man other than Rāghava dares to slay them.
t.1.18.12: For those two wicked ones, swollen with pride in their prowess, have fallen under the sway of the noose of Time; O tiger among kings, they are no match for the great-souled Rāma.
t.1.18.14: I know the great-souled Rāma, whose valor is true; so too does the greatly radiant Vasiṣṭha, and so do these others who abide in austerity.
t.1.18.13: O king, you ought not to show affection on account of your son. I give you my promise: know that those two rākṣasas are as good as slain.
t.1.18.15: If you desire for yourself the attainment of dharma and supreme, lasting fame on earth, O lord of kings, you ought to give Rāma to me.
t.1.18.16: O Kākutstha, if all your ministers, headed by Vasiṣṭha, give their consent, then send Rāma forth.
t.1.18.17: You ought to give me your beloved son, the unattached, lotus-eyed Rāma, for the ten nights of the sacrifice.
t.1.18.19: Having thus spoken these words, rich in dharma and in purpose, the righteous-souled Viśvāmitra, the great sage of mighty splendor, fell silent.
t.1.18.18: Act in such a way, O Rāghava, that the time of my sacrifice does not pass by. May good fortune be yours, and do not set your mind on grief.
t.1.18.20: Having heard those words of the sage, which pierced his heart and mind, the king fell into great fear; deeply distressed in mind, he trembled and slipped from his seat.
